requirements.name: workspace path normalization with separated execution and query modes
key UX: Every backend path-based Codex call goes through one shared workspace path strategy layer instead of each method deciding independently.
The strategy distinguishes execution calls from query calls so we do not reuse a history-specific fallback rule on mutating APIs.
The incoming workspace string remains the product-facing workspace identity while Codex-specific cwd variants are derived internally.

requirements.name: execution APIs use a single stable cwd candidate
key UX: thread/start, thread/resume, turn/start, thread/fork, and thread/rollback all use one shared execution cwd resolver.
On Windows, execution calls prefer the plain native drive path form such as D:\repos\My-Code-X-A because real Codex accepts it across the tested thread lifecycle APIs.
Execution calls do not retry with alternate cwd forms after success criteria are already clear, which keeps behavior deterministic and avoids hidden duplicate actions.

requirements.name: query APIs use plain-first fallback path matching
key UX: thread/list and thread history lookups try the plain Windows path first when a workspace is provided.
If the plain-path query succeeds and returns non-empty data, that result is authoritative and fallback stops immediately.
If the plain-path query succeeds but returns an empty list, the backend retries with the extended path form such as \\?\D:\repos\My-Code-X-A before treating the workspace as having no history.
If every supported path variant still returns empty data, only then does the product surface an empty history state.

requirements.name: history empty state reflects real empty results only
key UX: The thread history sidebar shows 'No thread history yet.' only after the full query path fallback sequence has been exhausted.
Users with existing threads under the same Windows workspace do not lose history because of an internal cwd representation mismatch.
Backend errors still surface as load failures rather than being silently converted into an empty state.

requirements.name: path strategy is observable in tests and diagnostics
key UX: Unit coverage verifies that Windows plain-path queries happen before extended-path fallback for history and thread list flows.
Regression tests verify that execution APIs keep working with the shared resolver and do not inherit query-only empty-result fallback behavior.
Optional debug logging can report which cwd variant was used for a query and whether fallback was triggered, without changing user-facing behavior.
